decision: Edit run-introspector HEARTBEAT.md step 3 (Triage) to add a tier-1 false-positive verification gate for exit_code=429 runs whose error_msg is substantive task output rather than a rate-limit banner
rationale:
Baseline: RUN_LESSONS.md entry 2026-04-23 (run `60116710`) documents that run-introspector spent a heartbeat investigating a successfully-completed investigation run that was misclassified as FAILED/429 because its assistant report discussed 'rate limit' as a topic. The substring matcher `detectRateLimit` in `scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/adapters/runner/claude_code.go:1518-1559` fires on any assistant text containing 'rate limit' regardless of IsError, forcing Success=false, ExitCode=429. Recent-failed-runs scan in that lesson confirms 2/22 (~9%) of FAILED runs match the pattern (ids `60116710`, `e08357a4`).

Current step 3 prose (run-introspector/HEARTBEAT.md): '3. **Triage.** Walk the ladder in order. At the first tier with a run not already in RUN_LESSONS.md, pick one. Stop walking the ladder.' This picks the contaminated tier-1 runs first every time they surface.

Proposed edit: replace step 3 with — '3. **Triage.** Walk the ladder in order. At the first tier with a run not already in RUN_LESSONS.md, pick one — but apply the **tier-1 false-positive gate** first: if the candidate is an errored run with exit_code == 429 AND the error_msg looks like substantive task output (multi-paragraph markdown with headings such as Summary / Classification / Report) rather than a terse rate-limit banner, reclassify it as tier-5 (random-success-with-misclassification), record the false-positive in RUN_LESSONS.md, and continue walking the ladder. Otherwise, stop walking. Rationale: detectRateLimit (claude_code.go:1518-1559) substring-matches "rate limit" anywhere in the final assistant message, so investigations whose reports merely discuss rate-limiting get misclassified — see RUN_LESSONS.md 2026-04-23 (`60116710`).'

Expected delta: tier-1 false-positive investigations drop from ~9% of picks to ~0%; ~1 wasted heartbeat per ~11 runs is recovered. Run-introspector still records the false-positive (so the misclassification rate stays measurable), but does not waste depth on it.

Measurement plan: (a) after merge, the next RUN_LESSONS.md entry that encounters a 429+substantive-text run should mark it 'tier-1 false-positive (skipped)' rather than open a full lesson on it; (b) grep RUN_LESSONS.md 7 heartbeats from now — count of tier-1 lessons opened on 429-completion-text runs should be 0; (c) when scenario-qa fixes detectRateLimit, the gate becomes a no-op (still correct, no rollback needed).

rationale:
Baseline: 25 of 98 successful runs in this heartbeat's window are `swarm-manager:initiative:rev-trigger:review:round-001` with wall-clock 70k–82k seconds. Spot-check of `564191ef-e1b4-4328-b21c-c83999676123` (wall-clock 81,648s, the longest) shows `last_heartbeat - started_at = 15s`, `summary.turns_used=1`, `summary.tokens_used=27523`, `summary.cost_estimate=$0.09`, `requires_approval=true`, and `ended_at == approved_at = 2026-04-24T21:09:57`. Identical agent work; wall-clock spread is ~6,000× because operator batch-cleared the approval queue at 21:09:5X UTC (25 runs ending within ~7s of each other). Wall-clock is therefore not a slow signal for sandboxed approval-required runs.

Current HEARTBEAT.md "Reasoning Framework" tier-3 prose: "Slow — run exceeded expected tokens or duration by > 50%". "Duration" is unqualified; natural reading is wall-clock.

Proposed edit: replace tier-3 line with — "3. **Slow** — run exceeded expected tokens or **work-duration** by > 50%. Work-duration = `last_heartbeat - started_at` (or equivalent agent-side span), NOT `ended_at - started_at`. When `resolved_config.requires_approval=true`, wall-clock includes operator approval latency and is not a slow signal. Also exclude candidates where `summary.turns_used <= 1` AND `summary.cost_estimate < $0.20` (a 1-turn cheap run is structurally not slow regardless of wall-clock)."

Expected delta: tier-3 picks no longer dominated by approval-queue artifacts. The current 25-run cluster falls out; future tier-3 picks reflect actual agent inefficiency.

Measurement plan: (a) 7 heartbeats from now (2026-05-01), grep RUN_LESSONS.md for any tier-3 lesson opened on a `requires_approval=true` run with `turns_used <= 1`. Expected count: 0. (b) When tier-3 next fires, the picked run should have `last_heartbeat - started_at` actually > 50% over expected.

Failure-mode check: (1) not polishing — concrete contamination affecting 25/98 runs in one window; (2) not sprawl — edit existing agent file; (3) not premature programmatic conversion — prose-to-prose; (4) not churn — clear baseline + delta; (5) not too-fast deprecation — improve, not prune; (6) in-lane — run-introspector observes, team-agent-optimizer implements (per RUN_LESSONS.md handoff convention); the underlying agent-manager `ended_at` semantics are explicitly NOT touched (correct as-is for audit); (7) not conversion-without-measurement — measurement plan above.

rationale:
Source: extended audit conversation 2026-05-04 against templates/scenarios/react-vite/. The seven existing audit-technique lenses (screaming-architecture, boundary-of-responsibility, seam-discovery, invariant, cognitive-load, decision-boundary, code-cleanup) had each been applied to the same template at various points without surfacing the kind of multiplier-aware findings that templates accumulate — per-replica cost of duplicated infrastructure, drift surfaces between future copies, contracts encoded in comments vs the type system, coordinated-edit count for adding/removing features. None of those are wrong-on-a-single-instance; they only become wrong when the artifact is replicated. The seven existing lenses ask 'is this code good?'; this lens asks the multiplier-aware question 'is this code good as a copy source?'

Option space:
- A. Place new doc in docs/scenario-qa/audit-techniques/ and tag the skill audit-technique. Cost: pollutes scenario-qa's registry with a lens quality-auditor doesn't use; misleads the qa-contrarian on regular-scenario audits.
- B. Create new registry folder docs/agent-system/audit-techniques/ + extend TECHNIQUE_REGISTRIES. Cost: registry-of-one is premature per Vrooli's 'don't extract until you see the pattern' rule.
- C (chosen). Standalone canon doc at docs/agent-system/REFERENCE_PATTERN_FITNESS.md + paired skill with non-audit-technique tag. Smallest move. agent_system_canon_test.sh ignores it (correctly — it's not in any registry). Promotion to a registry happens later when a second similar lens lands.

Applicability gate is the load-bearing field: lens applies only to artifacts that exist to be copied (templates, reference scenarios, canonical examples). Composes with single-instance lenses by running AFTER them on the same artifact, not instead of them. Multiplier-framed findings are only correct given that the artifact is otherwise structurally sound.

Worked example concrete: react-vite template audit produced 6 tiered findings (3 Tier-1 substrate candidates: CLI per-domain client boilerplate → cli-core, UI per-domain lib boilerplate → in-template lib/api.ts, route-vs-descriptor parity → module_test.go; 2 Tier-2: cli_commands_seed.json third source of truth, RepositoryCreateInput type-system contract; 1 Tier-3: endpoints.go description style consistency). Substrate-vs-template categorization (the strategic question): 2 of 6 needed cli-core substrate work, 4 of 6 fix in-template. The categorization is the lens's primary output.

Why this lens is owned by toolchain-validator and not quality-auditor: toolchain-validator already runs against the gold-star reference each heartbeat per its existing role; the reference is generated from a template; the template's quality bounds the reference's quality. Adding longer-cadence template audit to toolchain-validator's surface closes the previously-implicit operator-driven loop. quality-auditor stays on real scenarios where multiplier framing would mislead — its registry is untouched.

Why single registry expansion (REFERENCE_SCENARIOS.md) and not parallel template registry: templates and references are 1:1 in practice; two registries would force every change to touch both. Six-column shape (Role/Scenario/Template/Generated/Last audit/Notes) captures the pair as one entity. Adds drift detection for free — when template's last commit is newer than reference's Generated date, the reference may need regenerating; the new toolchain-violation subtype 'reference-stale-from-template' covers this fourth rot case.

Failure-mode check: (1) not polishing — concrete documented gap (six tiered findings the existing seven lenses missed); (2) not sprawl — supersedes-by-extension rather than stacks; new skill is scoped tightly via applicability gate; existing seven lenses untouched; (3) not premature programmatic conversion — prose-to-prose lens with paired procedural skill; (4) not churn-without-benefit — clear baseline (template→reference quality coupling currently implicit and operator-driven; making it explicit gives toolchain-validator the longer-cadence cycle the role description previously lacked) + measurement plan (each registered template gets a row, monthly cadence, findings linked from REFERENCE_SCENARIOS.md); (5) not too-fast deprecation — additive; (6) in-lane — meta-self-improvement is meta-optimization's owned context; team-agent-optimizer is the structural-changes role; (7) measurement: the next reference-react-vite scan should flag any new template-side findings via the new Last audit column staleness check.
